subject: maths
question: During the first year the population of a village increased by 5% and during the second year it diminished by 5%. At the end of the second year its population was 47,880. What was the population at the beginning of the first year?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = 5 − 5 − (5 × 5) ÷ 100 = −0.25%

Net population ratio = 100% − 0.25% = 99.75%

99.75% of population = 47,880

Initial population = 47,880 ÷ 0.9975 = 48,000

**∴ The correct answer is 48000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Final population = 47,880, **First year increase** = 5%, **Second year decrease** = 5%.

**Formula Used:** Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 − r₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97f0bd35458f5f5ac9ff15beca3bdd69790354aa60b19b078bb95b3a05b33600.png] 

⇒ Let the population at the beginning be P.

⇒ Population after 1st year = P × (1 + 5/100) = P × (105/100) = 21P/20

⇒ Population after 2nd year = (21P/20) × (1 − 5/100) = (21P/20) × (95/100) = (21P/20) × (19/20)

⇒ (21P/20) × (19/20) = 47,880

⇒ 399P / 400 = 47,880

⇒ P = (47,880 × 400) ÷ 399

⇒ P = 120 × 400 = 48,000

**∴ The correct answer is 48000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by x% and then y%, the net change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Population Growth Formula

The final population after n years with constant growth rate r is Pₙ = P₀(1 ± r/100)ⁿ.

Ratio Method for Percentages

A 5% increase corresponds to a ratio of 21/20, while a 5% decrease corresponds to a ratio of 19/20.</p
